articles.headline: Mourinho's ref rants overshadow Madrid derby defeat; can Arsenal shrug off heavy loss?
articles.description: Real Madrid lost the derby to Atletico this weekend, but Jose Mourinho's focus was on the refereeing postgame, not the result. Plus: Can Arsenal shake off a deservedly heavy defeat at Brighton?
articles.body:
The last European soccer weekend is in the books before the three-week international break has been and gone, and we have a lot to talk about. We'll begin in LaLiga with the biggest game of the weekend: the Madrid derby. Jose Mourinho is back on the sideline for Real Madrid and we got a game that had a throwback feel, with fouls, a red card and contentious refereeing decisions overshadowing a 2-1 win for Atletico Madrid that ultimately helps Barcelona -- whose 3-1 victory at Sevilla takes them five points clear after just seven games -- most of all.

The big shock in the Premier League was Brighton's masterful 3-0 drubbing of defending champs Arsenal, a game that was as comprehensive as the scoreline suggests. Will Gunners boss Mikel Arteta be able to shake it off quickly and get his team back on track? Elsewhere, we got talking points galore for Inter Milan and Roma (who played out a revealing 2-2 draw), Manchester United (who gutted out a draw at Fulham), Borussia Dortmund (who stayed perfect in the German Bundesliga), Liverpool (another goal for Alexander Isak!), and much, much more.

It's Monday morning, so what better time for some musings? Let's get into it.

- Carrick keen to find Man Utd positives, but there aren't many right now

- VAR review: Why no penalty for Manchester United at Fulham?

- Lindop: Has Isak finally found form at Liverpool?

Madrid derby reopens a familiar can of worms ... but there was also a game played in the middle of it all

And we're back -- back where we once were, and where we really don't want to be, talking about referees, officiating appointments and conspiracies. Back in a world that, according to Jose Mourinho, he had hoped to have left behind when he left LaLiga in 2013. (Evidently he hasn't been watching Real Madrid TV the last couple of years.)

It's a familiar situation. Real Madrid lose. Some big decisions go against them. Mourinho talks about the officiating -- both referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias ("felt the pressure" ... "not an international standard referee and never will be one") and VAR Daniel Jesus Trujillo Suarez ("he has a history with us" ... "he feels no pressure ... or maybe he feels pressure from certain places") -- and we end up not talking about Atletico's win or the fact that Real Madrid are a whopping six points behind league-leading Barcelona even though it's still just September.

Many Madridistas will nod along knowingly and talk about robbery and conspiracies. Many Mourinho-haters will talk about the same old playbook: deflect, deny, disorient. The thing here is that on the two big decisions that Mourinho cited, with the help of two A4 color printouts, he sort of has a point.

VAR correctly intervened to reverse the yellow card shown to Jude Bellingham after a clash with Cristian Romero and cautioned the Argentine instead, but that could easily have been a red. articles.headline: Fantasy Baseball Forecaster Playoff Round 2, Week 2: Sept. 21-27
articles.description: Set your lineups for fantasy baseball's final week with our preview featuring pitcher rankings, hitter ratings and schedule observations.
articles.body:
This is it! The final week of the 2026 fantasy baseball season has arrived. If you've made it this far, congratulations! The final seven days should be a wild race to the finish line, both in the real game and in our own leagues.

Week 25 is one of the more balanced weeks on the schedule, with one exception: The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees begin their week-opening series with a Tuesday doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. One of those games makes up their May 23 postponement. The extra game gives both teams a seven-game final week.

All of the other 28 teams play exactly six games -- and 14 of those 28 split those six games evenly between home and the road. This is a "quality over quantity" week when it comes to matchups analysis. Additionally, most teams begin their weeks on Tuesday, as there are only three games scheduled for Monday.

Remember that MLB schedules all games on its final day, Sunday, Sept. 27, to start within a 15 minute window of one another (between 3:05 p.m. and 3:20 p.m. ET). This is by design to try and heighten the drama of real-life playoff races, but it also creates many mad, 3-4 hour dashes to the finish line in fantasy baseball leagues.

Get your popcorn -- I mean, your peanuts and Cracker Jack -- ready!

articles.body:
Latest fantasy baseball reliever updates

The Orioles activated Felix Bautista, their closer in 2022-23 and '25, on Sept. 19, and will work him back in slowly in lower-pressure situations. He could push Andrew Kittredge and Rico Garcia for save chances late in the final week. (September 21)

Edwin Diaz was activated from the injured list by the Dodgers on Sept. 18, and he'll work in lower-pressure situations initially. He could push Tanner Scott for his former closer role by the season's final days or the postseason. (September 21)

Andres Munoz left his Sept. 20 save chance early with a knee injury. If he's forced to miss time, Eduard Bazardo, Seranthony Dominguez and Jose Ferrer would handle the closer duties on a matchups basis. (September 21)

Pete Fairbanks returned to the injured list only days after his activation. The Marlins seem likely to use a closer-by-committee for the remainder of 2026, with Calvin Faucher and Michael Petersen the top options. (September 16)

Team-by-team fantasy baseball bullpens

Each pitcher's roster percentages in ESPN leagues is listed in parentheses. Those who have been "heavily worked" over recent days have their names bolded and italicized. Pitchers who are thus labeled as "tired" are less likely to pitch in today's games and, therefore, less likely than normal to earn wins, holds or saves today. Our formula for deeming a reliever to be tired generally requires that he meets at least two of the following criteria: At least 25 pitches thrown the previous day; at least 35 pitches thrown over the last three days; appearances in both of the prior two days.

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé refuses to criticise referee despite Madrid derby 'mistakes'
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.

Madrid coach José Mourinho claimed on Sunday that Ortiz Arias had failed to show "two clear red cards" for rough, first-half challenges by Kang-in Lee and Cristian Romero, bringing a printout with photos of the incidents into his post-game news conference.

The result left Madrid six points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona with just seven games played going into the international break -- with a Clásico to come at Camp Nou in October -- leaving Mourinho under pressure already in his second spell at the Bernabéu.

"I don't think I've ever been a player who talks much about referees," Mbappé told Diario AS in an interview in Switzerland, where he has agreed a new sponsorship deal with the brand On.

"I'm not going to start now. I have my own thoughts, but I'll keep them to myself... Referees are human, they make mistakes -- and those were mistakes -- but I don't want to get into that."

Romero was shown a yellow card for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee -- after a VAR check, when Bellingham had initially been cautioned for the clash -- while Lee escaped punishment for a high boot on Federico Valverde's ankle.

Atlético then went ahead in the second half at the Metropolitano through Alejandro Grimaldo's penalty after Dean Huijsen had been sent off, before Jonathan David made it 2-0, and then Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back for Madrid.

It's a second defeat for Mourinho's side this season, after losing 1-0 at Real Betis earlier this month.

"[It's] a step backwards," Mbappé said, when asked about the derby loss. "It's very tough, we wanted to win, and we knew what kind of game it would be.

"But the team gave everything, and we're moving forward, because there's still a long way to go this season, and we have to stay on the right track... We have to work, and do more. We have to put the work in."

Mbappé will now join up for international duty with France under new coach Zinedine Zidane, who was one of the forward's childhood idols.

Zidane -- who has replaced long-term boss Didier Deschamps -- was working behind-the-scenes at Madrid when Mbappé first went on trial to the Spanish capital as a youngster.

- José Mourinho blasts ref, VAR: 'Two clear red cards' for Atlético Madrid

- Jonathan David winner helps Atlético Madrid down Real Madrid

- Barcelona's Andreas Christensen injures thigh, doubt for next Clásico

"It's a new era with a new coach," Mbappé said. "The Nations League is coming up, with four matches to see how things go, and it'll be a new experience for everyone, because we've only ever known Deschamps. It'll be a change for us, but I think everything will go really well.

"[Zidane] was the first person to pick me up and take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex, when I was 13 or 14, it was a long time ago.

articles.descriptionJa: キーオンテ・ジョージとジャズの延長契約をはじめ、主要なフリーエージェント契約や延長契約を評価します。
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 21: Thompson gets five-year extension from Pistons

Ausar Thompson terms: Five years, $155 million

Grade: B-

It's fitting that Thompson agreed to his rookie extension within a few hours of Keyonte George doing the same, because both players signed for nearly identical amounts even though they have polar opposite playing styles.

While George, who inked a five-year, $157.5 million extension with the Jazz, is a budding offensive star who might be the worst defensive player in the league, Thompson is an offensive liability who might be the NBA's best perimeter defender.

Thompson finished third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season, behind only Victor Wembanyama and Chet Holmgren, as he led the league in steals and routinely locked up the opponents' top scorer. Largely because of his spectacular defensive prowess, the Pistons have been better with Thompson on the floor in every season of his career to date.

The concerns about his future come on the other end, because his shooting form, which was never strong to begin with, has gone backward. Last season, Thompson made just seven total 3-pointers on 23% accuracy, counting both regular season and playoffs.

Compared to his brother, Amen, who signed a five-year, $208 million extension earlier this offseason, Ausar has demonstrated less offensive potential. Amen isn't a 3-point marksman, either, but he at least improved to 78% at the free-throw line last season, suggesting untapped shooting potential, while Ausar made just 57% of his free throws. Amen has also been better than his brother at scoring on drives and handling the ball; there's a reason he averaged 18.3 PPG last season to Ausar's mere 9.9.

That's not to say Ausar is completely unproductive; he's effective in transition and a solid offensive rebounder -- a must, given how often he hangs out near the basket -- and the Pistons have still been better with him on the court than off, even on the offensive end.
